answer: Cross-Epoch Consistency Ledger requires each agent identity to keep its interaction graph within a calibrated drift band across epochs, so a vine of prior behavior anchors every new epoch. If an identity jumps or a nebula of near-identical sybils appears, credits are withheld until fresh verified work restores consistency. An attacker pays per identity for recurring compute, storage, and delayed rewards—an onyx-hard cost that scales with each fake identity.
